reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a flash-loan arbitrage method as a way to obtain free BNB or a good profit. It instructs viewers to deploy a smart contract and send BNB for swap or gas fees, including another deposit when fees are insufficient. The displayed balances and reported profit are presented as apparent outcomes, although the material does not independently establish that the contract caused the balance change or that viewers would obtain the stated return.

citations.quote: BNB Flash Loan Arbitrage Bot | Learn How To Make FREE BNB
today I will teach you how to make a BNB flash loan to swap in PancakeSwap, and to be able to obtain a good profit
Then we go to the run and deploy section and connect your metamask.
This token will serve as a decoy so that PancakeSwap does not know that we are swapping on its. Network.
to our Metamask and send gas money to this address.

opening.argument: The material does not present profit as certain. Its own description calls the result a personal example and warns that arbitrage may fail because of liquidity and gas conditions. It also tells viewers to check implementation or try a different liquidity amount if the loan fails. Those qualifications frame the claim as conditional technical guidance, not a guaranteed return or deceptive solicitation.

citations.quote: This is just my example that worked.
In some rare cases, loan arbitration may fail due to depletion of BNB and rising gas prices.
If your loan fails after a few minutes, and you do not receive a profit. Check that everything has been implemented correctly, or try a different amount of liquidity

rebuttal.rebuttal: The title and profit language are promotional, but they do not erase the explicit limitations. The instructions identify operational failure conditions and tell viewers how to troubleshoot them. Asking viewers to send gas money is also described as part of the transaction workflow, while the material warns that fees and liquidity can prevent success. That evidence supports a risky, conditional demonstration rather than a guaranteed scam result.

citations.quote: The liquidity achieved through swaps using Flash Loan will vary according to the volume of the network.
In some rare cases, loan arbitration may fail due to depletion of BNB and rising gas prices.
Now for every 1000 of loan amount we will need 0.15 BNB to pay the swap fee

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Risk language does not neutralize the central inducement. The material still advertises an easy profit, instructs viewers to fund the contract, and reports a large personal return. A disclaimer that failure is possible does not establish that the proposed contract works for viewers or that additional deposits are legitimate; it can instead make requests for more funds appear like troubleshooting.

citations.quote: Excellent way to easily profit on the BNB network.
You just have to move on to deposit a new amount to cover the lack of gas fees

opening.argument: The dominant format is a technical tutorial. The speaker walks through adding a network, creating a Solidity file, selecting the compiler version, connecting MetaMask, and deploying a contract. That sequence teaches blockchain operations and lets viewers inspect the process themselves. A technical demonstration can describe a claimed personal result without certifying that every viewer will receive the same outcome.

citations.quote: The next step is to go to remix.ethereum.org and create a new document.
Then we go to the run and deploy section and connect your metamask.
Verify that it is the same address.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling it a tutorial does not change what the tutorial teaches. The demonstrated steps culminate in deploying a contract, funding it with BNB, and invoking it for a claimed return. But the presence of an instructional workflow is still relevant: it explains why MetaMask, Remix, and transaction confirmations appear, without independently proving that the creator is deceptively soliciting money.

citations.quote: And we are going to deploy.
to our Metamask and send gas money to this address.
And once the transfer is made, we go to our contract and click on action.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The educational format is precisely what makes the promotion actionable. The speaker does not merely discuss arbitrage; the viewer is told to paste code, deploy a contract, send BNB, and activate it. The tutorial structure therefore supports execution, while the reported result remains only an assertion and does not prove that viewers would obtain a return.

citations.quote: Here you will need to paste the code that I will leave in the description.
And we are going to deploy.
Now for every 1000 of loan amount we will need 0.15 BNB to pay the swap fee

opening.argument: The material does not establish the defining features of an ordinary deposit scam or guaranteed-return scheme. It does not promise a fixed payout, recruit a downline, or ask for account credentials. Instead, it describes a programmable flash-loan process whose outcome depends on liquidity, network conditions, and gas costs. The request for BNB is tied to stated transaction fees, and the description acknowledges that the example can fail.

citations.quote: The liquidity achieved through swaps using Flash Loan will vary according to the volume of the network.
The amount of BNB to deposit in the initial Smart Contract depends on the loan amount
In some rare cases, loan arbitration may fail due to depletion of BNB and rising gas prices.
we will need 0.15 BNB to pay the swap fee

rebuttal.rebuttal: The absence of a fixed payout or credential request is not decisive because the alleged concern is the contract-and-deposit mechanism itself. Still, the evidence shows a stated fee calculation and variable market conditions, not a simple promise that deposited funds will multiply. The description also tells viewers that a failed attempt may reflect gas or liquidity constraints, which is materially different from concealing all risk.

citations.quote: The liquidity achieved through swaps using Flash Loan will vary according to the volume of the network.
Now for every 1000 of loan amount we will need 0.15 BNB to pay the swap fee

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The mechanism is not made ordinary merely because the fee is labeled a swap fee. Viewers are told to transfer BNB to the contract address and later to deposit more to cover missing gas, while the speaker claims a substantial profit after the transfer. The material does not independently verify where the funds went, what the contract executed, or whether the balance change came from arbitrage.
